repositories.brief_summary: Uchar gained ASCII/Latin-1 helper functions, a Weak.get_copy continuation-safety fix landed, and several typing soundness bugs were fixed on trunk.
repositories.new_features_summary: New Uchar.{is_ascii,ascii_to_char,is_latin1,latin1_to_char} functions and a musl signal-stack sizing fix merged to trunk.
repositories.new_features:
- New `Uchar.is_ascii`, `Uchar.ascii_to_char`, `Uchar.is_latin1`, and `Uchar.latin1_to_char` functions were merged, clarifying the ambiguous latin1-vs-ASCII behaviour of the existing `Uchar.is_char`/`Uchar.to_char` (now deprecated in their favour) ([#14981](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14981), closing [#14962](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14962)), by [@copy](https://github.com/copy).
- `Weak.get_copy` no longer shallow-copies continuations, fixing a segmentation fault that could occur when a weakly-held continuation was duplicated and both copies were resumed ([#14988](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14988)) by [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop).
- The runtime now sizes the alternate signal stack from `sysconf(_SC_MINSIGSTKSZ)` when available, fixing a fatal "Failed to allocate signal stack" error on musl libc 1.2.6+ on certain Intel CPUs ([#14933](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14933)) by [Nat Mote](https://github.com/nmote), merged with review from [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron).
- `printast` now prints a trailing newline after `Pexp_unreachable`, fixing malformed AST dumps ([#14992](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14992)) by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27).
- The let-rec check now gives generic (unknown-type) arrays dynamic size, fixing a segfault on 32-bit systems where flat float arrays and boxed arrays have different word sizes but were previously assumed to have the same static size ([#14993](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14993)) by [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop).
- A soundness bug allowing `Obj.magic`-style casts via abstract types defined by module `include` was fixed, removing the wrong assumption that abstract types defined in the current module are always injective ([#14982](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14982)) by [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop).
- The build now requires and generates `configure` with Autoconf 2.72, gaining large-file (LFS) and year-2038 (`_TIME_BITS=64`) support checks and updated C++-compiler detection ([#14953](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14953), addressing [#14937](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14937)) by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27).
- The Makefile now avoids a build-reproducibility race where `otherlibs/str` and `otherlibs/unix` `.cmi`/`.cmx` files could be compiled from two different rules recording different source paths, changing interface digests non-deterministically ([#14989](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14989)) by [Bernhard M. Wiedemann](https://github.com/bmwiedemann), cherry-picked to the 5.5 branch by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27).
repositories.activity_summary: Sixteen PRs opened this week span atomic-operation codegen, a Weak.Make rewrite, Hashtbl reimplementation, and typing-internals refactoring.
repositories.activity:
- [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA) opened two configure-related PRs following up on the Autoconf 2.72 switch: defaulting to large-file and year-2038 support on 32-bit systems ([#14997](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14997)) and switching C++ compiler detection to Autoconf's own machinery to fix a `-std=gnu23` flag conflict ([#14996](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14996)), plus a set of small Cygwin build fixes ([#14921](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14921)).
- [Jacques Garrigue](https://github.com/garrigue) opened a draft simplifying `enforce_current_level` to avoid a spurious `unify_var` call ([#14995](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14995)), and follow-ups to the injectivity fix: removing the now-redundant `in_current_module`/`in_pervasives` helpers ([#14990](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14990), folded into [#14982](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14982)) and a draft making abstract types defined directly in structures injective ([#14991](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14991)).
- [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) opened a PR generating native atomic exchange/compare-and-set instructions across amd64, arm64, riscv, POWER, and s390x for immediate-typed atomics, avoiding the C call and its write barrier when the payload is known non-pointer, with per-architecture hardware benchmarking ([#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14980), follow-up to [#14575](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14575)); they also reviewed [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm)'s stack-reallocation size PR ([#14812](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14812)) with detailed notes on RISC-V displacement limits.
- [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) opened a rewrite of `Weak.Make` ("weak hashsets") using open-addressing with linear probing instead of bucket arrays, reporting a 30% speedup on an alt-ergo benchmark and up to 2.8x on some ocaml-hashcons workloads ([#14979](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14979)), and continued discussion on enabling `-g` by default in the bytecode compiler ([#14971](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14971)) and disabling a benchmark mistakenly run as a test ([#14960](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14960)).
- [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) opened a change making `Runtime_events.User.write` non-allocating by replacing a per-domain closure-based write-buffer cache with a single atomic bytes slot in DLS, removing roughly 23 words of allocation per event ([#14984](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14984)), discussed with [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5).
- [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop) also opened a fix so the expansiveness check considers effect-handler cases, fixing a segfault from an unhandled expansive allocation inside an `effect` match case ([#14986](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14986)).
- [Alistair](https://github.com/johnyob) opened a PR adding typing support for optional polymorphic parameters, encoding them as `Tpoly` under an option type ([#14985](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14985)), discussed with [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron) and [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate).
- Ongoing typing-internals refactoring continued with [Samuel Vivien](https://github.com/samsa1)'s merge of `eqtype` with `moregen` ([#14739](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14739)) and the change to make `unify` return a `result` rather than raise ([#14425](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14425)), alongside [Jacques Garrigue](https://github.com/garrigue)'s fix for the `type_newtype` regression reported in [#14842](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14842) ([#14983](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14983)).
- Other open work under review this week includes [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist)'s POWER frame-pointer support ([#14505](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14505)), [agrn](https://github.com/agrn)'s comballoc peephole optimisation merging pointer-bump instructions ([#14812](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14812)), [shym](https://github.com/shym)'s relocatable cross-compiler support ([#14929](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14929)), [Jeannalyse](https://github.com/Jeannalyse)'s draft reimplementation of `Hashtbl` with deterministic iteration order via dynamic arrays ([#14956](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14956)), and [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes)'s proof-of-concept moving systhreads into the runtime ([#14965](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14965)).
- Stdlib feature-wish PRs continued to accumulate review, including [Khalid](https://github.com/khalidbelk)'s `Sys.filepath_exists` ([#14974](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14974)), [Brian Ward](https://github.com/WardBrian)'s `Result.all`/`Option.all` ([#14964](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14964)), [Benoit](https://github.com/benjub)'s `Char.Ascii.is_punct` ([#14957](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14957)), and [Jeannalyse](https://github.com/Jeannalyse)'s `Atomic.compare_and_exchange` ([#14912](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14912)).
repositories.discussions_summary: Discussion focused on an atomic-locs soundness hole in polymorphic record fields and diagnosing a typechecker crash regression.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) reported that `[%atomic.loc]` on a polymorphic record field can be used to implement `Obj.magic`, producing a genuine unsoundness ([#14987](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14987)); [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) analysed the typing gap around `Tpoly` instantiation for atomic-record primitives.
- The `Ctype.Unify` typechecker crash reported by [Eduardo Souza](https://github.com/udesou) ([#14842](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14842)) drew a multi-round discussion between [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel) and [Jacques Garrigue](https://github.com/garrigue) about where `update_level`/`enforce_current_level` should be called around locally-abstract module scopes, resulting in the fix PR [#14983](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14983) and the related simplification [#14995](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14995).
- [Török Edwin](https://github.com/edwintorok) raised that `int Atomic.t` still emits polling points and a C call to `caml_atomic_fetch_add_field` instead of inlined machine instructions ([#14976](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14976)), motivating a companion PR exposing that `Atomic.t` is not a float in the `.mli` ([#14977](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14977)) and connecting to [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham)'s native atomic-exchange/CAS work ([#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14980)).
repositories.trends_summary: Continued push to replace C-call atomics with inlined native instructions, and multiple bugs this week were found with LLM assistance.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Several fixes credited LLM-assisted bug discovery, including the injectivity soundness fix ([#14982](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14982)), the effect-case expansiveness fix ([#14986](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14986)), the `Weak.get_copy` continuation fix ([#14988](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14988)), and the win32 select handle leak fix ([#14975](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14975)), each disclosed per the project's AI policy.
- Atomic-operation performance work is converging on inlining native instructions in place of C calls when the payload type is statically known non-pointer, spanning fetch-and-add (referenced from [#14575](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14575)), exchange/compare-and-set ([#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14980)), and `.mli` type exposure to aid the optimizer ([#14977](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14977)).
- Reworking of core data structures for both performance and determinism continued with a `Weak.Make` open-addressing rewrite ([#14979](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14979)) and a `Hashtbl` reimplementation targeting deterministic iteration order ([#14956](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14956)).
- Build-system hygiene work is ongoing around the Autoconf 2.72 migration, with follow-up PRs for large-file/year-2038 support ([#14997](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14997)) and C++ compiler detection ([#14996](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14996)) landing the same week as the base switch ([#14953](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14953)).

repositories.brief_summary: Kate opened two fixes for safe_mode cache handling in sandboxed environments after a bug report from dinosaure.
repositories.activity_summary: Two new PRs address sandboxed safe_mode cache handling, tracked against a switch-invariant fix and a git-maintenance race report.
repositories.activity:
- Two PRs were opened by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) directly in response to a sandboxing bug report: one makes `OpamCached` **respect `safe_mode`** instead of unconditionally removing an outdated cache file ([#7067](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7067)), and the other makes `opam init --reinit` **regenerate the list of valid switches and their cache** rather than leaving stale entries, also adding `$PWD` to the switch list when it is a valid switch and pruning invalid ones ([#7068](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7068)); both track the underlying report at [#7066](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7066).
- [R. Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou) reviewed [#7067](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7067), asking for a **dedicated safe_mode test** since there is currently no full safe-mode test coverage, and reviewed the unrelated in-flight `opam init --reinit` retry-prompt fix ([#7058](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7058)), flagging a missing changelog entry.
- Issue [#6982](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6982) (`opam switch import` not exporting the switch **invariant**) was closed this week.
- Discussion continued on the `opam repo add` **git-maintenance race condition** ([#7031](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7031)), with [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) distinguishing a TOC/TOU issue in `OpamSystem` that would need a mutex around `.git/objects/maintenance.lock` from a separate git bug already fixed upstream in git 2.55.
- The **checksum-for-opam-file** feature wish ([#5932](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5932)) picked up a comment from [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) pointing to an existing `opam-ed`-based workaround in [kit-ty-kate/opam-alpha-repository](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate/opam-alpha-repository).
repositories.discussions_summary: Sandboxed use of opam's internal libraries and a git-maintenance race in `opam repo add` were the week's notable discussion threads.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Calascibetta Romain](https://github.com/dinosaure) (robur) reported that opam's `OpamCoreConfig`/cache-removal behavior breaks tools that introspect the current switch from a **sandboxed, read-only context**, since opam unconditionally tries to delete an outdated package cache ([#7066](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7066)); [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) triaged this into two concrete fixes ([#7067](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7067), [#7068](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7068)).
- On [#7031](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7031), [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) separated the `opam repo add` failure into two distinct causes — an opam-side time-of-check/time-of-use race with git's own maintenance lock file, and a git bug already fixed in git 2.55 that GitHub Actions' bundled git (2.54) still hits.
repositories.trends_summary: Cache and switch-state correctness in edge-case environments (sandboxes, concurrent git access) is a recurring theme this week.
repositories.emerging_trends: - Multiple threads this week concern **cache and switch-state correctness in non-standard environments**: sandboxed read-only tooling ([#7066](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7066), [#7067](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7067), [#7068](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7068)), concurrent git access during repository updates ([#7031](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7031)), and incomplete state export on `opam switch import` ([#6982](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6982)).
repositories.contributors_summary: Kate authored two bug-fix PRs and triaged/commented on three issues; rjbou reviewed both in-flight PRs; dinosaure and Khady filed reports.
repositories.contributors:

repositories.brief_summary: emre closed several long-standing client-capability issues while rgrinberg extracted shared Lsp library helpers and expanded e2e test coverage.
repositories.new_features_summary: Client-capability-aware fixes landed for document symbols, diagnostic tags, folding ranges, semantic highlighting, hover, and definition requests.
repositories.new_features:
- Document symbol kinds now respect the client's `textDocument.documentSymbol.symbolKind.valueSet`, falling back to `Constructor` and `Class` for clients that only support the original protocol kinds, by [emre](https://github.com/dayangac) ([#2122](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2122), fixes [#2121](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2121))
- Diagnostics now carry `Unnecessary` and `Deprecated` tags so editors can grey out unused values and strike through deprecated ones, by [emre](https://github.com/dayangac) ([#2110](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2110), fixes [#2109](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2109))
- Workspace-symbol responses honor `SymbolTag.Deprecated` support, emitting the modern tag while keeping the legacy `deprecated` field as a fallback, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#2113](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2113))
- Folding ranges now respect `FoldingRangeClientCapabilities`, omitting character positions for `lineFoldingOnly` clients, omitting the `Region` kind when unsupported, and truncating to `rangeLimit`, by [emre](https://github.com/dayangac) ([#2099](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2099), fixes [#911](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/911))
- Semantic highlighting now classifies module names in `with` constraints (`S with module M = N`) and in signature `open`s, which previously received no token, by [emre](https://github.com/dayangac) ([#2098](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2098), fixes [#808](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/808))
- Hovering a variant constructor or exception at its declaration site now reports its type instead of returning nothing, by [emre](https://github.com/dayangac) ([#2102](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2102), fixes [#1300](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1300))
- Definition, declaration and type-definition requests return an empty result instead of an error when Merlin cannot resolve the cursor position (e.g. on a keyword), removing spurious error notifications in editors, by [emre](https://github.com/dayangac) ([#2100](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2100), fixes [#1161](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1161))

repositories.brief_summary: Dune saw allocation-focused performance work across the engine and fiber scheduler, new allocation-profiling traces, and a 3.24.2 patch release.
repositories.new_features_summary: New `--split-public-names` describe flag, batch/watch status-line timing, and allocation-profiling traces landed alongside broad perf work.
repositories.new_features:
- `dune describe` gains a `--split-public-names` flag for `workspace` and `external-lib-deps` that reports private names in `name`/`names` and public names separately in new `public_name`/`public_names` fields, and now defaults to reporting an executable's public name instead of its private one, by [Nat Karmios](https://github.com/NatKarmios) ([#15582](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15582), addressing [#15497](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15497))
- Batch-mode builds now display **build duration** and **average process parallelism** in the status line, and watch-mode status lines show the currently running build, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15564](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15564), [#15673](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15673))
- Status-line build **parallelism** is now derived from process CPU time rather than wall-clock action time (Windows keeps wall-clock time) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15685](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15685))
- New **allocation profiling** support: setting `DUNE_TRACE=+alloc` records sampled allocation profiles in traces, configurable via the experimental `DUNE_TRACE_ALLOC` variable (`rate`, `stack`, `top`), attributing exact GC-counter totals to call stacks, allocation sites and inclusive stack frames, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15699](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15699), [#15703](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15703), [#15710](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15710), [#15738](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15738))
- Dune traces now also record per-build **Memo** compute/restore/cycle-detection metrics ([#15698](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15698)) and discovered/validated/failed **rule counts** ([#15701](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15701)), by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)
- Fixed `js_of_ocaml` libraries with no implementation (or interface-only modules) being rebuilt on every invocation instead of being cached, by [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro) ([#15427](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15427))
- Fixed filesystem trace metrics for file writes and directory scans, and preserved runtime-event ring IDs so trace consumers can distinguish interleaved event streams, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15686](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15686), [#15687](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15687))
- Extensive **performance work** landed across the build pipeline: the fiber scheduler was rewritten to represent continuations and computations explicitly instead of via closures ([#15723](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15723)), with further allocation reductions in digesting ([#15727](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15727), [#15731](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15731), [#15741](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15741)), path/string handling ([#15688](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15688), [#15694](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15694), [#15739](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15739), [#15740](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15740)), the engine/memo layer ([#15672](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15672), [#15705](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15705), [#15711](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15711), [#15715](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15715), [#15726](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15726), [#15742](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15742), [#15747](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15747)) and major GC frequency ([#15730](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15730)), by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)

repositories.discussions_summary: Discussions covered per-package LICENSE installs, a menhir/package-management build failure, and maintenance_intent syntax.
repositories.notable_discussions:

repositories.brief_summary: The 'Implicit source positions' RFC from Olivier Nicole ([#52](https://github.com/ocaml/RFCs/issues/52)) saw an update while remaining open for review.
repositories.activity_summary: The open 'Implicit source positions' RFC by Olivier Nicole was updated, proposing a `[%call_pos]` arrow type for automatic call-site tracking.
repositories.activity: - The **'Implicit source positions' RFC** ([#52](https://github.com/ocaml/RFCs/issues/52)), opened by [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole) on behalf of Tarides and Jane Street, remains open and was updated this week; it proposes a new `[%call_pos]` arrow type so that a labeled function parameter of type `Lexing.position` is automatically filled with the call site's location when not explicitly supplied, intended to improve stack-trace-free tracing of monadic binds, testing frameworks, and error reporting in embedded languages.
repositories.contributors_summary: Olivier Nicole continued stewarding the open 'Implicit source positions' RFC.
repositories.contributors: - [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole) authors and maintains the **'Implicit source positions' RFC** ([#52](https://github.com/ocaml/RFCs/issues/52)), which documents a design (implemented and used internally at Jane Street, originally prototyped by [Frédéric Bour](https://github.com/let-def) and revived by [Lucas Pluvinage](https://github.com/TheLortex)) for automatically capturing call-site source positions via a `[%call_pos]` labeled argument.

repositories.brief_summary: Functor lookup through `module type of` fixed in the cross-referencer, alongside driver work on Findlib path inference and OCaml 5.6 support.
repositories.new_features_summary: Cross-referencer now resolves functors reached via `module type of`, fixing a spurious xref warning ([#1471](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1471)).
repositories.new_features:
- Fixed **identifier lookup for functors** reached indirectly through `module type of` (e.g. `module Named : module type of Make`), which previously produced a spurious "Failed to lookup type identifier" warning; `handle_apply` in `src/xref2/tools.ml` was rewritten to reuse `expansion_of_module` and match on its `Functor`/`Signature` result rather than re-implementing functor-chasing, and the unused `` `UnresolvedOriginalPath `` error variant was removed from `src/xref2/errors.ml` by [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) ([#1471](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1471))
- Added a cram test (`test/xref2/functor_type_of.t`) covering the `module type of` functor-resolution case, including exclusion of the invalid `struct include Functor(Module) end` form ([#1471](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1471))
- `odoc driver` now infers library/stdlib directories using Findlib's own path-resolution logic instead of hardcoding a subpath of the opam prefix, which was breaking on setups like openSUSE Tumbleweed where the stdlib lives under `lib64` rather than `lib/ocaml`, by [@katrinafyi](https://github.com/katrinafyi) ([#1474](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1474), not yet merged)
- Test matrix for GitHub Actions updated in `.github/workflows/build.yml` by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([#1473](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1473))
- CHANGES.md updated to record the functor-lookup fix ahead of the next release ([#1471](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1471))

repositories.brief_summary: A draft PR was opened to build js_of_ocaml against Introcaml-instrumented OCaml switches, prompting discussion on introspection support (#2409).
repositories.activity_summary: A draft PR opened by Frédéric Bour adds compatibility stubs so js_of_ocaml builds against Introcaml-instrumented OCaml switches (#2409).
repositories.activity:
- [Frédéric Bour](https://github.com/let-def) opened a **draft PR** adding the adaptations needed for js_of_ocaml to build against the `5.5.0+introcaml` opam switch, an experimental OCaml compiler extension that instruments values for runtime printability; the changes ignore a new field in `Const_block`, ignore a new `NEXT_RESERVED_BITS` instruction, and provide stubs for a few new runtime primitives ([#2409](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/pull/2409))
- The PR remains open and unmerged as the maintainers weigh the deployment story for supporting an instrumented switch before Introcaml itself is upstreamed ([#2409](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/pull/2409))
repositories.discussions_summary: Maintainer feedback on #2409 questioned whether jsoo should support value introspection and how to scope new runtime primitives.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [@hhugo](https://github.com/hhugo) asked whether there is a plan for js_of_ocaml to support introspection and pretty-printing of values, in response to [Frédéric Bour](https://github.com/let-def)'s Introcaml compatibility PR ([#2409](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/pull/2409))
- [@hhugo](https://github.com/hhugo) suggested annotating the new Introcaml-related primitives with `//If: introspect` so they don't bloat the runtime for toplevel and separate-compilation builds that currently include all primitives ([#2409](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/pull/2409))

repositories.brief_summary: AVX512 backend/mask-load-store support landed alongside alloc-mode-for-returns and several typing soundness fixes.
repositories.new_features_summary: AVX512 mask load/store primitives, alloc mode for returns, and named binders for DWARF shapes landed this week.
repositories.new_features:
- **AVX512 backend support** merged in stages by [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat): backend groundwork ([#6339](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6339)), array primitives ([#6340](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6340)), a beta extension surface ([#6676](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6676)), and new `Pstring_load_mask`/`Pbytes_load_mask`/`Pbigstring_load_mask` (and matching `_set_mask`) primitives for masked vector load/store ([#6708](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6708))
- New **`return_mode`** type (`Maybe_alloc_stack` / `Not_alloc_stack`) added to `lambda.mli` alongside `return_mode_to_locality_mode`, implementing **alloc mode for function returns** by [ainageorges](https://github.com/ainageorges) ([#5877](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5877))
- **Named binders for shapes** improve DWARF/debugging output by [Simon Spies](https://github.com/spiessimon) ([#5111](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5111))
- Fixed **unsound function argument/return sorts** in partial GADT matches by [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([#6689](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6689))
- Forbade `[%atomic.loc]` and mutable indices on **polymorphic record fields** where the representation is undetermined, closing a soundness gap by [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([#6688](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6688))
- Fixed a **speculative inlining** bug where the code size of non-lifted closures was counted twice by [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) ([#6705](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6705))
- Fixed **code size estimation of mergeable switches** by [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp) ([#6737](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6737))
- `Persistent_env.compute` now strips excess arguments by [Zesen Qian](https://github.com/riaqn) ([#6729](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6729)), and bound-identifier stamps are normalized when saving a `.cmi` to improve reproducibility ([#6542](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6542))
- **`ocamlfrontend`** split out from `ocamlcommon` as a separate library, changing build/debug directory layout (see updated `HACKING.md`) by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27-js) ([#6470](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6470))
- **Runtime contention fixes** by [Stephen Dolan](https://github.com/stedolan) ([#6719](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6719))
- Series of amd64 **peephole optimizations** by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc): `neg` instruction for integer negation ([#6701](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6701)), removing redundant sign/zero extensions ([#6703](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6703)), removing a redundant `test` after `and`/`or`/`xor` ([#6722](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6722)), avoiding zero materialization for `vsqrtsd`'s merge operand ([#6702](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6702)), and folding `Cconst_natint` constants into immediate operands during CFG selection ([#6704](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6704))
- Simplifier now collapses `compare x y = 0` directly into an equality comparison by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) ([#6723](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6723))
- **CFG invariants strengthened** to catch backend bugs earlier by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) ([#6371](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6371))
- Regalloc validator now costs `Equation_set.union` by overlap rather than by size, improving validation performance by [@julesjacobs](https://github.com/julesjacobs) ([#6686](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6686))
- Merlin updated for `5.4.0-ox4` by [Liam Stevenson](https://github.com/liam923) ([#6683](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6683)), with a follow-up fix for jump-to-definition ([#6694](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6694)) and unmerging of comments ([#6684](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6684))
- `HACKING.jst.md` documentation updated to reflect the merlin refresh by [Liam Stevenson](https://github.com/liam923) ([#6734](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6734))
repositories.activity_summary: 24 PRs opened this week remain open, spanning reaper link-time optimization, runtime effects, and allocation-mode-axis work.
repositories.activity:
- Newly opened work not yet merged includes **addressable kinds**, a new-language-feature typing proposal by [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([#6712](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6712)), and related record label-access sharing ([#6698](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6698))
- **Reaper link-time optimization** progressed with naive dependency-graph merging in the `-reaper-solve` entrypoint and solve plumbing opened by [Miriam Vellacott](https://github.com/mirivella) ([#6731](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6731), [#6725](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6725)), building on the open reaper tracking issue ([#5267](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5267)) and unnecessary kind-registering removal merged by [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) ([#6691](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6691))
- **Runtime effects/dynamic-binding** work opened by [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat): lexical dynamic parents ([#6710](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6710)), storing dynamic bindings outside `stack_info` ([#6709](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6709)), and freezing/shifting dynamic tables ([#6711](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6711)), following earlier closed attempts at lexical fiber parents ([#6652](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6652)) and inheritable dynamics ([#6381](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6381))
- **Allocation mode axis** design opened by [zhizhuoxin](https://github.com/zhizhuoxin) ([#6733](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6733)), following a closed testing variant ([#6727](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6727)) and two merged prerequisite fixes: forcing local allocation for noalloc functions ([#6548](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6548)) and an allocation-mode-axis fix for multi-argument functions and partial application ([#6452](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6452))
- **Flambda2 bit-counting and arithmetic optimizations** opened by [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp): new primitives for `clz`/`ctz`/`popcnt` ([#6738](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6738)) and rewriting single-arm switches to `apply_cont` ([#6736](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6736)), with a matching simplifier constant-folding extension opened by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) ([#6726](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6726)) and a fuse of float-comparison tagging into one operation ([#6728](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6728))
- **Zero-alloc annotation tracking** via `alloc_regions` opened by [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) ([#6730](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6730)), alongside a merged fix for `One_bit_fewer` machine-width handling by [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp) ([#6690](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6690)) and cmx-loading profiling additions ([#6714](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6714))
- **Cost-metrics accuracy for closures containing stubs** tracked in a new issue by [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) ([#6720](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6720)), closing out the related closed issue on set-of-closures cost metrics fixed via [#6737](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6737) ([#5141](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5141))
- Testsuite and tooling changes opened this week include a prototype `Translquotes` implementation by [Jakub Bachurski](https://github.com/jbachurski) ([#6732](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6732)), removal of runtime-5 markers by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) ([#6707](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6707)), a bytecode-typing-info drop option by [Stephen Dolan](https://github.com/stedolan) ([#6706](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6706)), `ocamltest` `set`/`split` interaction fix by [Luke Maurer](https://github.com/lukemaurer) ([#6721](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6721)), and DWARF test argument filtering for runtime C functions by [Stephen Dolan](https://github.com/stedolan) ([#6717](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6717))
- Merged cleanup work included removal of unused `toplevel_my_region`/`toplevel_my_ghost_region` by [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) ([#6716](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6716)), simplification of rec-info aliases by [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp) ([#6715](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6715)), general flambda2 dead-code removal ([#6713](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6713)), stale CR removal in codegen tests ([#6700](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6700)), a `Cconst_natint` peephole fold ([#6704](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6704)), and the `ocamlformat` enablement in `camlinternalQuote` by [Jakub Bachurski](https://github.com/jbachurski) ([#6577](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6577))
- `module type of` typechecking skips a vacuous nongen check for persistent modules, fixed by [@julesjacobs](https://github.com/julesjacobs) ([#6685](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6685)), and dunelike/ocamltest infrastructure was updated to match parameterised-library builds and variable-expanded action names ([#6693](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6693), [#6425](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6425))
- `[max_int + 1]` overflow to `min_int` in integer literals disallowed by [James Rayman](https://github.com/jra4) ([#6670](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6670)), and a lazy-renaming-during-import issue was opened by [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp) ([#6695](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6695))
- Dependency maintenance: GitHub Actions bumped across four updates via dependabot ([#6699](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6699)), and `Btype.hash_variant` moved to `Obj` as an upstream OCaml backport by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27-js) ([#6692](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6692))
repositories.trends_summary: Backend micro-optimization by one contributor and multi-stage feature rollout (AVX512, reaper, effects) by others dominated the week.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- A steady stream of small, tightly-scoped **amd64 peephole and CFG optimizations** tagged `100% vibe` came from [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) ([#6701](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6701), [#6702](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6702), [#6703](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6703), [#6704](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6704), [#6722](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6722), [#6723](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6723), [#6371](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6371), [#6680](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6680), [#6700](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6700), [#6728](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6728), [#6726](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6726)), indicating an ongoing incremental codegen-quality push
- Large features continue to land as **multi-PR sequences** rather than single patches, seen in AVX512 (four PRs: [#6339](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6339), [#6340](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6340), [#6676](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6676), [#6708](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6708)) and runtime effects/dynamic-binding work (three open PRs: [#6710](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6710), [#6709](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6709), [#6711](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6711))
- **Allocation-mode axis** work is being iterated through repeated close/reopen cycles ([#6727](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6727) closed, [#6733](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6733) opened; [#5110](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5110) closed) as [zhizhuoxin](https://github.com/zhizhuoxin) and [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) converge on a design
- Typing soundness bugs around **partial GADT matches and polymorphic record fields** were fixed in the same week, both by [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([#6689](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6689), [#6688](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6688)), suggesting ongoing hardening of the unboxed-types/record-representation area

repositories.activity_summary: New PR relaxing opam version guards for dune, eio and mdx, plus continued discussion on mdx OxCaml compatibility.
repositories.activity:
- [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) opened a PR to **relax opam version guards**, allowing upstream `>=dune 3.24.2`, `>=eio.1.4` and `>=mdx.2.6.0` to be installable now that these releases build correctly with OxCaml, which unblocks his website monorepo build against the `5.2.0minus39` OxCaml switch ([#59](https://github.com/oxcaml/opam-repository/issues/59))
- Discussion continued on the ongoing PR marking **mdx.2.6.0 as OxCaml-compatible** by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27-js), which tracks the upstream fix in [ocaml/opam-repository#30305](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30305) ([#55](https://github.com/oxcaml/opam-repository/issues/55))
- [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) confirmed that **dune 3.24.2 merged upstream** into the ocaml/opam-repository and opened a follow-on PR there ([ocaml/opam-repository#30398](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30398)), needed to fully close out [#55](https://github.com/oxcaml/opam-repository/issues/55)
repositories.discussions_summary: Investigation of an unrelated wasm backend CI failure and cross-repo coordination on mdx compatibility timing.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- On [#59](https://github.com/oxcaml/opam-repository/issues/59), [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) flagged what appears to be an **unrelated CI failure** in `compiler/lib-wasm/link.ml`, an inexhaustive pattern-match warning on `Config.effects ()` surfacing during the `runtime-cps.wasm` build rule
- On [#55](https://github.com/oxcaml/opam-repository/issues/55), [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) noted that the **mdx fix would appear in dune 3.24.2**, which [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) then confirmed had merged upstream, tying the OxCaml-side PR to progress in [ocaml/opam-repository#30305](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30305) and [ocaml/opam-repository#30398](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30398)
repositories.trends_summary: Version guards in opam metadata are being relaxed as upstream packages (dune, eio, mdx) gain OxCaml compatibility.

- Tight **coordination with the upstream ocaml/opam-repository** project, with fixes tracked jointly across repositories ([ocaml/opam-repository#30305](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30305), [ocaml/opam-repository#30398](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30398))

repositories.contributors:

- [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) commented on [#55](https://github.com/oxcaml/opam-repository/issues/55) to clarify that the mdx fix would ship in dune 3.24.2

repositories.brief_summary: Windows path support merged via `Eio.Path.native`, plus a new `of_dir` helper and unified `dir_path` handling across backends.
repositories.new_features_summary: Windows native-path support merged with `Eio.Path.of_dir`, contravariant `Path.t`, and a 32-bit build fix.
repositories.new_features:
- Windows path support implemented as an `Eio.Fs.Pi` backend, adding an `Nt_path` module that handles Windows volume prefixes, drive-relative paths, and `\\?\`/`\??\` NT paths for `join`/`split`, closing the long-standing tracking issue [#762](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/762) by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5), building on work started by [Kento Okura](https://github.com/kentookura) in [#738](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/738) ([#916](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/916))
- New `Eio.Path.of_dir` function returns an empty path relative to a directory, avoiding manually constructed `(dir, "")` tuples, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#919](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/919))
- `Eio.Path.t` is now contravariant (`-'a t` instead of `'a t`), a step toward eventually making `Path.t` private, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#919](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/919))
- `dir_path` representation for the current directory and filesystem root unified to always use `""` instead of mixing `""` in `eio_linux` and `"."` in `eio_posix`, fixing inconsistent native-path printing for the subtree `"./."`, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#920](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/920))
- Fixed `eio_posix` build failure on 32-bit architectures where `MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC` did not fit in an OCaml `int`, by moving the check into C, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5), reported by [Stéphane Glondu](https://github.com/glondu) ([#917](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/917), fixes [#909](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/909))
- Added POSIX and Windows path tests, merging duplicated cases into `tests/fs.md` so Windows-specific `Nt_path` logic is also exercised on Linux and macOS, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#918](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/918), [#916](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/916))
repositories.activity_summary: Draft device-node and mock-directory PRs from prior weeks stayed open while the Windows path-handling series merged.
repositories.activity:

- **Windows path-handling series** completed this week: [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) merged the `Eio.Path.native` Pi backend and `Nt_path` module ([#916](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/916)), the `Eio.Path.of_dir` helper ([#919](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/919)), and the `dir_path` cleanup that followed from review of [#919](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/919) ([#920](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/920)), closing the tracking issue for Windows path handling ([#762](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/762))
- [Kento Okura](https://github.com/kentookura)'s earlier draft PR implementing native Windows paths was closed as its approach was incorporated into [#916](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/916) ([#738](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/738))
- **32-bit build support** restored with [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5)'s fix for the `MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC` constant reported by [Stéphane Glondu](https://github.com/glondu) ([#917](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/917), [#909](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/909))
- POSIX path test consolidation merged, reducing duplication between existing and newly added test cases ([#918](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/918))
repositories.discussions_summary: Windows path semantics, including drive-relative paths and NT path prefixes, were debated at length on the native-path PR.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- Extended review discussion on [#916](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/916) between [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) over how Win32 resolves drive-relative paths like `C:foo` (via process cwd or a hidden per-drive environment variable maintained by `cmd.exe`), concluding such paths should be treated as rooted and rejected in sandboxed operations, with a request for confirmation from [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27)
- Discussion of the distinction between the `\\?\` and `\??\` NT path prefixes and why the `is_step`/`is_relative` naming needed to change once join logic moved into the `Pi` layer, on [#916](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/916)
- Mid-review CRLF/LF line-ending problems while converting Windows path tests to mdx format were tracked back to a known `mdx` issue (`realworldocaml/mdx#294`) before being partly reverted, on [#916](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/916)
- [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) noted on [#914](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/914) that a zero-allocation `runtime_events` write API requested for `Eio.Private.Trace` is now up for review upstream at [ocaml/ocaml#14984](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14984)
repositories.trends_summary: Work continues consolidating around finishing Windows platform support and unifying path-handling abstractions across backends.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Continued push toward full **Windows platform support**, spanning the long-running tracking issue ([#125](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/125)), the now-closed path-handling tracking issue ([#762](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/762)), and the native-path implementation ([#916](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/916))
- Incremental **consolidation of the `Path`/`Fs.Pi` abstraction**, with `of_dir` ([#919](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/919)) and `dir_path` unification ([#920](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/920)) both aimed at reducing backend-specific special cases ahead of a possible future move to a private `Path.t`
- Test consolidation trend, merging platform-specific path tests into shared `tests/fs.md` so Windows path logic is exercised on Linux/macOS CI too ([#918](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/918), [#916](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/916))
repositories.contributors_summary: talex5 merged the Windows path-handling series and a 32-bit build fix while avsm advanced draft device and mock PRs and reviewed path semantics.
repositories.contributors:

- [Thomas Gazagnaire](https://github.com/samoht) reported an issue on `Eio.Private.Trace` allocating 23 words per event while the `runtime_events` ring is active, with a minimal reproduction case ([#914](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/914))

group_summaries.cross_repository_work:

group_summaries.emerging_trends:
- **[ocaml/opam-repository](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository)**: [Dmitrii Kosarev](https://github.com/Kakadu) is systematically migrating packages with disappeared or unstable upstream archives onto a dedicated **opam-source-archives** GitHub mirror, covering `coq-lsp`, `curses`, `pgsolver`, `simlog`, `pxshot`, `vecosek`, and `rfsm`, closing several bad-checksum reports along the way ([ocaml/opam-repository#30241](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30241), [ocaml/opam-repository#30244](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30244), [ocaml/opam-repository#30240](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30240))
- **[ocaml/opam-repository](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository)**: new-package submissions are commonly iterated through several closed-then-reopened PRs before merging as CI feedback drives version bumps, seen with **soteria**, **hegel**, **p4spectec**, and **ocaml-neo4j-driver** ([ocaml/opam-repository#30438](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30438), [ocaml/opam-repository#30423](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30423), [ocaml/opam-repository#30430](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30430), [ocaml/opam-repository#30448](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30448)), while others like **par** ([ocaml/opam-repository#30429](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30429)) never make it through
- **[ocaml/ocaml.org](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org)**: metadata-presentation work is increasingly framed around avoiding misleading not just human readers but also search crawlers and LLMs about which package versions are current, as reflected in the accessibility and semantic-labelling work in [ocaml/ocaml.org#3713](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3713)
- **[ocaml/ocaml.org](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org)**: content/event pages continue to be kept in sync with real-world logistics (venue confirmation, registration going live, CFP closing) close to the event date, as seen in the OCaml Workshop 2026 updates ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3734](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3734))

group_summaries.new_features_summary: New Uchar.{is_ascii,ascii_to_char,is_latin1,latin1_to_char} functions and a musl signal-stack fix merged in ocaml/ocaml; no RFCs features this week.
group_summaries.new_features:
- New `Uchar.is_ascii`, `Uchar.ascii_to_char`, `Uchar.is_latin1`, and `Uchar.latin1_to_char` functions were merged, clarifying the ambiguous latin1-vs-ASCII behaviour of the existing `Uchar.is_char`/`Uchar.to_char` (now deprecated in their favour) ([ocaml/ocaml#14981](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14981), closing [ocaml/ocaml#14962](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14962)), by [@copy](https://github.com/copy).
- `Weak.get_copy` no longer shallow-copies continuations, fixing a segmentation fault that could occur when a weakly-held continuation was duplicated and both copies were resumed ([ocaml/ocaml#14988](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14988)) by [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop).
- The runtime now sizes the alternate signal stack from `sysconf(_SC_MINSIGSTKSZ)` when available, fixing a fatal "Failed to allocate signal stack" error on musl libc 1.2.6+ on certain Intel CPUs ([ocaml/ocaml#14933](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14933)) by [Nat Mote](https://github.com/nmote), merged with review from [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron).
- `printast` now prints a trailing newline after `Pexp_unreachable`, fixing malformed AST dumps ([ocaml/ocaml#14992](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14992)) by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27).
- The let-rec check now gives generic (unknown-type) arrays dynamic size, fixing a segfault on 32-bit systems where flat float arrays and boxed arrays have different word sizes but were previously assumed to have the same static size ([ocaml/ocaml#14993](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14993)) by [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop).
- A soundness bug allowing `Obj.magic`-style casts via abstract types defined by module `include` was fixed, removing the wrong assumption that abstract types defined in the current module are always injective ([ocaml/ocaml#14982](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14982)) by [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop).
- The build now requires and generates `configure` with Autoconf 2.72, gaining large-file (LFS) and year-2038 (`_TIME_BITS=64`) support checks and updated C++-compiler detection ([ocaml/ocaml#14953](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14953), addressing [ocaml/ocaml#14937](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14937)) by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27).
- The Makefile now avoids a build-reproducibility race where `otherlibs/str` and `otherlibs/unix` `.cmi`/`.cmx` files could be compiled from two different rules recording different source paths, changing interface digests non-deterministically ([ocaml/ocaml#14989](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14989)) by [Bernhard M. Wiedemann](https://github.com/bmwiedemann), cherry-picked to the 5.5 branch by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27).
group_summaries.group_overview:
- Activity was concentrated in [ocaml/ocaml](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml), with sixteen new PRs opened this week; [ocaml/RFCs](https://github.com/ocaml/RFCs) saw a single RFC update.
- New stdlib helpers (`Uchar.is_ascii`/`Uchar.ascii_to_char`/`Uchar.is_latin1`/`Uchar.latin1_to_char`, [ocaml/ocaml#14981](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14981)) and several typing-soundness and memory-safety fixes landed on trunk, including an abstract-type injectivity fix ([ocaml/ocaml#14982](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14982)) and a `Weak.get_copy` continuation-safety fix ([ocaml/ocaml#14988](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14988)).
- Native atomic exchange/compare-and-set codegen ([ocaml/ocaml#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14980)) and a `Weak.Make` open-addressing rewrite ([ocaml/ocaml#14979](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14979)) were opened, continuing performance-focused work from prior weeks.
- In [ocaml/RFCs](https://github.com/ocaml/RFCs), the 'Implicit source positions' RFC ([ocaml/RFCs#52](https://github.com/ocaml/RFCs/issues/52)) by [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole) was updated while remaining open for review.
group_summaries.activity_summary: Sixteen PRs opened in ocaml/ocaml spanning atomic codegen, Weak.Make/Hashtbl rewrites, and typing-internals refactors; the RFCs proposal was updated.
group_summaries.activity:
- [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA) opened two configure-related PRs following up on the Autoconf 2.72 switch: defaulting to large-file and year-2038 support on 32-bit systems ([ocaml/ocaml#14997](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14997)) and switching C++ compiler detection to Autoconf's own machinery to fix a `-std=gnu23` flag conflict ([ocaml/ocaml#14996](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14996)), plus a set of small Cygwin build fixes ([ocaml/ocaml#14921](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14921)).
- [Jacques Garrigue](https://github.com/garrigue) opened a draft simplifying `enforce_current_level` to avoid a spurious `unify_var` call ([ocaml/ocaml#14995](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14995)), and follow-ups to the injectivity fix: removing the now-redundant `in_current_module`/`in_pervasives` helpers ([ocaml/ocaml#14990](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14990), folded into [ocaml/ocaml#14982](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14982)) and a draft making abstract types defined directly in structures injective ([ocaml/ocaml#14991](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14991)).
- [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) opened a PR generating native atomic exchange/compare-and-set instructions across amd64, arm64, riscv, POWER, and s390x for immediate-typed atomics, avoiding the C call and its write barrier when the payload is known non-pointer, with per-architecture hardware benchmarking ([ocaml/ocaml#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14980), follow-up to [ocaml/ocaml#14575](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14575)); they also reviewed [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm)'s stack-reallocation size PR ([ocaml/ocaml#14812](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14812)) with detailed notes on RISC-V displacement limits.
- [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) opened a rewrite of `Weak.Make` ("weak hashsets") using open-addressing with linear probing instead of bucket arrays, reporting a 30% speedup on an alt-ergo benchmark and up to 2.8x on some ocaml-hashcons workloads ([ocaml/ocaml#14979](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14979)), and continued discussion on enabling `-g` by default in the bytecode compiler ([ocaml/ocaml#14971](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14971)) and disabling a benchmark mistakenly run as a test ([ocaml/ocaml#14960](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14960)).
- [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) opened a change making `Runtime_events.User.write` non-allocating by replacing a per-domain closure-based write-buffer cache with a single atomic bytes slot in DLS, removing roughly 23 words of allocation per event ([ocaml/ocaml#14984](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14984)), discussed with [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5).
- [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop) also opened a fix so the expansiveness check considers effect-handler cases, fixing a segfault from an unhandled expansive allocation inside an `effect` match case ([ocaml/ocaml#14986](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14986)).
- [Alistair](https://github.com/johnyob) opened a PR adding typing support for optional polymorphic parameters, encoding them as `Tpoly` under an option type ([ocaml/ocaml#14985](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14985)), discussed with [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron) and [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate).
- Ongoing typing-internals refactoring continued with [Samuel Vivien](https://github.com/samsa1)'s merge of `eqtype` with `moregen` ([ocaml/ocaml#14739](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14739)) and the change to make `unify` return a `result` rather than raise ([ocaml/ocaml#14425](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14425)), alongside [Jacques Garrigue](https://github.com/garrigue)'s fix for the `type_newtype` regression reported in [ocaml/ocaml#14842](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14842) ([ocaml/ocaml#14983](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14983)).
- Other open work under review this week includes [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist)'s POWER frame-pointer support ([ocaml/ocaml#14505](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14505)), [agrn](https://github.com/agrn)'s comballoc peephole optimisation merging pointer-bump instructions ([ocaml/ocaml#14812](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14812)), [shym](https://github.com/shym)'s relocatable cross-compiler support ([ocaml/ocaml#14929](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14929)), [Jeannalyse](https://github.com/Jeannalyse)'s draft reimplementation of `Hashtbl` with deterministic iteration order via dynamic arrays ([ocaml/ocaml#14956](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14956)), and [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes)'s proof-of-concept moving systhreads into the runtime ([ocaml/ocaml#14965](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14965)).
- Stdlib feature-wish PRs continued to accumulate review, including [Khalid](https://github.com/khalidbelk)'s `Sys.filepath_exists` ([ocaml/ocaml#14974](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14974)), [Brian Ward](https://github.com/WardBrian)'s `Result.all`/`Option.all` ([ocaml/ocaml#14964](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14964)), [Benoit](https://github.com/benjub)'s `Char.Ascii.is_punct` ([ocaml/ocaml#14957](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14957)), and [Jeannalyse](https://github.com/Jeannalyse)'s `Atomic.compare_and_exchange` ([ocaml/ocaml#14912](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14912)).
- In [ocaml/RFCs](https://github.com/ocaml/RFCs), the 'Implicit source positions' RFC ([ocaml/RFCs#52](https://github.com/ocaml/RFCs/issues/52)), opened by [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole) on behalf of Tarides and Jane Street, was updated; it proposes a `[%call_pos]` arrow type so a labeled `Lexing.position` parameter is automatically filled with the call site's location when not explicitly supplied, aimed at stack-trace-free tracing of monadic binds, testing frameworks, and error reporting in embedded languages.
group_summaries.notable_discussions:
- [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) reported that `[%atomic.loc]` on a polymorphic record field can be used to implement `Obj.magic`, producing a genuine unsoundness ([ocaml/ocaml#14987](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14987)); [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) analysed the typing gap around `Tpoly` instantiation for atomic-record primitives.
- The `Ctype.Unify` typechecker crash reported by [Eduardo Souza](https://github.com/udesou) ([ocaml/ocaml#14842](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14842)) drew a multi-round discussion between [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel) and [Jacques Garrigue](https://github.com/garrigue) about where `update_level`/`enforce_current_level` should be called around locally-abstract module scopes, resulting in the fix PR [ocaml/ocaml#14983](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14983) and the related simplification [ocaml/ocaml#14995](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14995).
- [Török Edwin](https://github.com/edwintorok) raised that `int Atomic.t` still emits polling points and a C call to `caml_atomic_fetch_add_field` instead of inlined machine instructions ([ocaml/ocaml#14976](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14976)), motivating a companion PR exposing that `Atomic.t` is not a float in the `.mli` ([ocaml/ocaml#14977](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14977)) and connecting to [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham)'s native atomic-exchange/CAS work ([ocaml/ocaml#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14980)).
group_summaries.emerging_trends:
- Several fixes credited LLM-assisted bug discovery, including the injectivity soundness fix ([ocaml/ocaml#14982](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14982)), the effect-case expansiveness fix ([ocaml/ocaml#14986](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14986)), the `Weak.get_copy` continuation fix ([ocaml/ocaml#14988](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14988)), and the win32 select handle leak fix ([ocaml/ocaml#14975](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14975)), each disclosed per the project's AI policy.
- Atomic-operation performance work is converging on inlining native instructions in place of C calls when the payload type is statically known non-pointer, spanning fetch-and-add (referenced from [ocaml/ocaml#14575](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14575)), exchange/compare-and-set ([ocaml/ocaml#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14980)), and `.mli` type exposure to aid the optimizer ([ocaml/ocaml#14977](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14977)).
- Reworking of core data structures for both performance and determinism continued with a `Weak.Make` open-addressing rewrite ([ocaml/ocaml#14979](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14979)) and a `Hashtbl` reimplementation targeting deterministic iteration order ([ocaml/ocaml#14956](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14956)).
- Build-system hygiene work is ongoing around the Autoconf 2.72 migration, with follow-up PRs for large-file/year-2038 support ([ocaml/ocaml#14997](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14997)) and C++ compiler detection ([ocaml/ocaml#14996](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14996)) landing the same week as the base switch ([ocaml/ocaml#14953](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14953)).

weekly_summary.activity:

- __RUMINANT:core__ [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) opened a change making `Runtime_events.User.write` non-allocating by replacing a per-domain closure cache with a single atomic bytes slot in DLS, removing roughly 23 words of allocation per event [ocaml/ocaml#14984](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14984), discussed with [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5).

weekly_summary.notable_discussions:
- __RUMINANT:core__ [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) reported that `[%atomic.loc]` on a polymorphic record field can be used to implement `Obj.magic`, a genuine unsoundness [ocaml/ocaml#14987](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14987); [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) analysed the typing gap around `Tpoly` instantiation for atomic-record primitives.
- __RUMINANT:core__ The `Ctype.Unify` typechecker crash reported by [Eduardo Souza](https://github.com/udesou) [ocaml/ocaml#14842](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14842) drew a multi-round discussion between [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel) and [Jacques Garrigue](https://github.com/garrigue) about where `update_level`/`enforce_current_level` should be called around locally-abstract module scopes, resulting in the fix [ocaml/ocaml#14983](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14983).
- __RUMINANT:core__ [Török Edwin](https://github.com/edwintorok) raised that `int Atomic.t` still emits polling points and a C call instead of inlined machine instructions [ocaml/ocaml#14976](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14976), motivating [ocaml/ocaml#14977](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14977) and connecting to [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham)'s native atomic-exchange/CAS work [ocaml/ocaml#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14980).
- __RUMINANT:ecosystem__ [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) questioned why creating a second opam switch with OCaml 5.5.0 triggered a full compiler rebuild instead of reusing a relocatable build, closed after being unable to reproduce consistently [ocaml/opam-repository#30407](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30407).
- __RUMINANT:ecosystem__ A three-year-old request from [Jacob Reinhold](https://github.com/jcreinhold) to stop hardcoding `cc` in the `conf-openblas` build (instead honoring `$CC`) was closed this week [ocaml/opam-repository#23495](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/23495).
